one_liner: Zendesk has a broad REST API with OAuth2 (global OAuth for multi-customer apps); API tokens are being deprecated, and access requires a 14-day trial or paid account, with no free tier.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (with PKCE) is recommended. Multi-customer apps must use a global OAuth client, which has to be requested from Zendesk. API tokens (used via Basic auth as email/token:api_token) still work but are being removed: unused tokens deactivate from July 28, 2026 and all stop by April 30, 2027. Sunshine Conversations uses its own API keys with Basic auth or JWT.
access_notes: There is a free 14-day trial. Sponsored accounts are for Marketplace partners only. Customer developers should use their own instances or sandboxes. Some APIs need higher plans, such as Suite Growth for ZIS and Suite for Profiles. A global OAuth client for distribution has to be requested through Zendesk's marketplace process.
blocker_notes: There is no free tier, only a 14-day trial or a paid plan. Distributing to multiple customers needs a global OAuth client from Zendesk. Developer terms bar using customers' API tokens or their own OAuth clients.

evidence.quote: If you plan on distributing an app, integration, or bot to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests.
Starting July 28, 2026, unused tokens will automatically deactivate. By April 30, 2027, all API tokens will stop working.
use basic authentication with your email address and password, your email address and an API token, or an OAuth access token.
